title: EMV Additional Information Data Layouts
applicability: Applies to the repeating EMV Additional Information Section (Elements 191/192/118) carried in Data Segment 130 (request) and 131 (response).
source: docs/specs/extracted_text.txt Appendix T-1 through T-2; Element 191/192/118 main-body definitions.

businessRequirements.title: EMV Additional Information Indicator (Element 191) shall be exactly 3 numeric digits and equal to 001 or 002.
EMV Additional Information Length (Element 192) shall be exactly 3 numeric digits in the range 001-985.
The Table ID embedded at the start of EMV Additional Information (Element 118) shall equal the Indicator (Element 191) value.
EMV Additional Information Table ID 001 (EMV Table Data) shall carry exactly 6 characters equal to EMVYES or EMVNOT.
EMV Additional Information Table ID 002 (CARC) shall carry exactly 1 character identifying the Card Authentication Results Code returned by Visa in Bit No. 44.8.
The "Table Length" field described in Appendix T-1/T-2 shall conform to a stated digit count/value.
EMV Table Data (Table ID 001) included in an authorization response shall be echoed back on any subsequent advice or batch-upload request.

testCases.positive: Embedded Table ID equals Indicator value
Table ID 001 value is EMVYES or EMVNOT
Table ID 002 value is exactly 1 character
Response EMV Table Data is echoed into required follow-up advice/batch-upload request
negative: changed EMV Table Data on echo

testData.reason: Indicator=001 is a valid, fully synthesizable code.
Indicator=002 is valid per Appendix T's own Table ID 002 definition, reconciling Element 191's incomplete Valid Codes/Values list.
Indicator=003 is well-formed but not a defined Table ID.
Non-numeric indicator violates the 3-digit numeric format.
Length=006 is within the stated 001-985 range.
Length=000 is below the stated minimum of 001.
Length=986 exceeds the stated maximum of 985.
Embedded Table ID 002 does not equal Indicator 001.
Always REVIEW_REQUIRED by design; Appendix T-1/T-2 describe the "Table Length" column only as n/Fixed with no stated digit count or value anywhere in the appendix.
EMVYES is a valid Table ID 001 value.
EMVNOT is a valid Table ID 001 value.
Table ID 001 with a value other than EMVYES/EMVNOT is not defined.
A 1-character value satisfies the stated CARC length; the concrete code catalog is not given anywhere in Appendix T and is out of scope.
A 2-character value violates the stated 1-character CARC length.

Always REVIEW_REQUIRED by design; echoing a response's EMV Table Data into a subsequent advice/batch-upload request is a cross-message consistency rule that cannot be assessed from a single snapshot, mirroring Appendix R's cross-field BR.

testDataReadinessSummary.note: All seven BRs are backed by AppendixTEmvAdditionalInformationOracle and AppendixTEmvAdditionalInformationOracleTest (22 unit tests). No cryptographic material is involved; the two always-REVIEW_REQUIRED BRs are deterministic by design (no stated Table Length digit count, and cross-message echo cannot be assessed from one snapshot).

testDataStatus: AppendixTEmvAdditionalInformationOracle implements bounded, structural checks for all seven BRs: Indicator (Element 191) 3-digit numeric format restricted to 001/002 (reconciling Element 191's own incomplete Valid Codes/Values list against Appendix T's authoritative two-table definition and the spec's appendix-overview text), Length (Element 192) 3-digit numeric format in range 001-985, embedded Table ID agreement with the Indicator, Table ID 001 EMVYES/EMVNOT value format, and Table ID 002 one-character CARC format. "Table Length" field width and response-to-advice/batch-upload echo remain REVIEW_REQUIRED because neither is stated with enough precision in Appendix T to assert independently.
remaining: If BUYPASS/Visa ever states a concrete digit count or value for the "Table Length" column in Appendix T-1/T-2, encode it as a new BR.

Resolve EMV Table Data echo verification across authorization response and subsequent advice/batch-upload request if a concrete cross-message test harness is ever built - not assertable from a single snapshot today.
If a concrete CARC code catalog (values returned in Bit No. 44.8) is ever published, encode it as a closed-set BR instead of the current 1-character format-only check.
